messages:
Jordan (CS): Raising an escalation — enterprise customer (Acme Retail) reports repeated duplicate completions when their client tries to reconnect to our streaming endpoint after a network blip. They say sometimes they get partial output, then on reconnect they receive the remainder plus a full repeated completion. Billing complaint too: charged for tokens twice.
Emma (Support): @Jordan can you paste the exact repro steps the customer used? also which SDK/version? :thinking_face:
Jordan (CS): Here's their simplified repro (copied from customer):
1) open SSE to /v1/streams?model=redwood-llama-13b, no idempotency header
2) receive a few "data:" events (partial chunks)
3) client disconnects (mobile on flaky cell)
4) client reconnects and re-issues same request
Result: sometimes they receive the remaining tokens (expected resume), other times they get a full new generation appended (duplicate).
Emma (Support): SDK is their own JS client using EventSource polyfill. They didn't set any unique request id in headers.
Liam (Eng): Quick notes: current streaming implementation is best-effort resume for prefix cache if the reconnect arrives with a resume_token we issued. Otherwise we treat as a fresh request. We do not dedupe purely identical requests unless the client supplies an Idempotency-Key on the non-streaming call. Streaming behavior historically not covered.
Rebecca (Infra): Logs from the cluster for one of their reconnects:
```
[2026-05-01T18:20:11Z] conn_id=svc-22 stream_start req_id=abc123 socket=10.3.5.9
[2026-05-01T18:20:21Z] conn_id=svc-22 chunk seq=1 token_count=48
[2026-05-01T18:20:23Z] conn_id=svc-22 disconnect reason=network-reset
[2026-05-01T18:20:29Z] new_conn req_meta:(no idempotency, no resume_token)
[2026-05-01T18:20:30Z] new_conn matched model variant v1 -> spawn new generation req_id=def456
[2026-05-01T18:20:33Z] new_conn chunk seq=0 token_count=120 -> user sees duplicate
```
Jordan (CS): They also recorded the SSE frames; here's an example snippet they sent: 
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq":1,"text":"The quick brown"}

event: chunk
data: {"seq":2,"text":" fox jumps"}

// disconnect here

event: chunk
data: {"seq":0,"text":"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"}
```
Emma (Support): So sometimes server resumes (gives seq 3 onwards) and sometimes restarts from seq 0. Makes sense based on logs.
Liam (Eng): Two different failure modes: 1) reconnect with resume_token -> server reattaches to existing generation and continues (idempotent resume); 2) reconnect without resume_token -> server starts a new generation. The customer expects resume semantics when they reconnect with the same request, but their client doesn't include any resume token or request id.
Nora (PM): Customer expectation note: many mobile clients will automatically retry after a disconnect without preserving in-memory resume tokens. For UX we might need a client-driven recommended approach or server-side safeguards to avoid billing duplicates.
Jordan (CS): Customer asked: can we detect duplicates server-side and avoid charging twice? They want a fast patch or guide.
Rebecca (Infra): Short term mitigation: we can add a lightweight heuristics layer — when a new streaming request arrives from same API key within X seconds and the model/params/body match and we still have a warm generation in cache, we can return a resume_token hint and attach instead of starting a new generation. But edge cases: legitimate concurrent requests from same API key.
Liam (Eng): Implementation notes: we can match on a hash of request payload + model + streaming params + user_ip (optional) and check active generations that have not completed and whose last_emitted_seq < threshold. If match and client sends header X-Resume-Request: 1, we can attempt reattach. For dedupe/billing we should require a client-provided request id or Idempotency-Key for guaranteed semantics.
Emma (Support): Customer reacted: they're not able to change client to persist resume tokens but can send an Idempotency-Key per logical user action (UUID) and include it on reconnect attempts. They asked whether Idempotency-Key will prevent duplicate billing for streaming reconnects.
Liam (Eng): Right now Idempotency-Key is enforced on non-streaming generate endpoints and dedupes replayed requests within 24h. We don't honour it for streaming reconnects today. We can extend server to index active stream requests by Idempotency-Key if provided in initial connect metadata. That would give strong dedupe semantics: if reconnect uses same Idempotency-Key, we attach/reject duplicate generation.
Jordan (CS): Can we do this fast? customer needs something within 48 hours ideally.
Rebecca (Infra): Quick patch plan (48h):
- accept Idempotency-Key and optional Resume-Token in stream connect headers
- on connect, check active_stream_index for matching Idempotency-Key -> if exists, reattach and respond with `event: resume_confirm` and last_seq
- if no match but resume_token present, try to reattach by token lookup
- otherwise start new generation as today
Caveats: will add a new small in-memory index per region; memory bounded and TTL'd. Auditing/billing will mark tokens consumed by generation; if user reattaches we won't double-bill.
Liam (Eng): Also suggest we emit server-side event `event: dedupe_note` when we detect duplicate attempt so logs are clear. And add a billing flag so charge only when generation completes or when we confirm new generation started.
Emma (Support): For the customer, recommended immediate workaround: have client send a short-lived Idempotency-Key for each user action (UUID) and include it on reconnect attempts. If they can't modify client, we can enable heuristics on their API key for a temporary window.
Nora (PM): Action items: Jordan to communicate workaround + timeline. Engineering: Liam + Rebecca to own quick patch prototype. Emma to monitor billing impact. I'll schedule a follow-up in 24 hours.
Liam (Eng): I'll drop a minimal spec here (proto):
```
CONNECT /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx
Idempotency-Key: 6a1f9b2a-...
Resume-Token: r123 (optional)
```
Server responses: on successful reattach:
```
event: resume_confirm
data: {"last_seq":2,"resume_token":"r123"}

event: chunk
data: {"seq":3,"text":"over the lazy dog"}
```
On duplicate attempt rejected: `event: duplicate_rejected` (client should then fetch last state rather than assume new generation).
Jordan (CS): I'll share the spec with customer and flag the temporary heuristics. I'll also ask for a client-side trace (EventSource logs) to confirm correspondence.
OpsBot: Incident created INC-2026-0427 streaming-dup-billing, priority=P2, assignee=@Liam (Eng)
Rebecca (Infra): I'll prototype the in-memory index and TTL logic; should be safe to ship behind a feature flag.
Emma (Support): Customer confirmed they can add Idempotency-Key on reconnect in their next deploy; they asked if we'll roll the server patch gracefully — yes?
Liam (Eng): We'll roll behind FF, enable for that customer only first, monitor errors and billing metrics. Plan: patch + canary in 48-72h, wider rollout after validation.
Nora (PM): Thanks team. Jordan please update customer with the workaround + expected timeline and ask them to tag us if they see duplicates after we enable the flag.
Jordan (CS): Will do. Closing loop in 12 hours with status update. :white_check_mark:
